candidate.answerReason: Integer-coefficient factorization forces both 9 and 105 to divide a, hence 315 divides a. An explicit integer-coefficient polynomial attains a = 315.

methods.label: Obtain a divisibility bound and attain it
methods.explanation:
Since \(a=P(1)\), the number \(a\) is a positive integer. The four equal values at odd inputs mean that \(P(x)-a\) has roots \(1,3,5,7\). Factoring out these roots gives
\[
P(x)-a=A(x)Q(x),
\]
where
\[
A(x)=(x-1)(x-3)(x-5)(x-7)
\]
and \(Q(x)\) has integer coefficients. To justify the coefficient condition, division by a monic factor \(x-k\), with integer \(k\), preserves integer coefficients; each remaining distinct root remains a root of the quotient.

At the even inputs, \(P(x)-a=-2a\). Evaluating at \(4\) and \(8\) yields
\[
-2a=9Q(4),\qquad -2a=105Q(8).
\]
Thus \(9\) and \(105\) divide \(2a\). Both are relatively prime to \(2\), so both divide \(a\). Therefore
\[
\operatorname{lcm}(9,105)=315
\]
divides \(a\), proving \(a\geq315\).

We must also show that \(315\) is attainable. For \(a=315\), the required even-input values of \(Q\) are determined by
\[
\begin{aligned}
(A(2),A(4),A(6),A(8))&=(-15,9,-15,105),\\
(Q(2),Q(4),Q(6),Q(8))&=(42,-70,42,-6).
\end{aligned}
\]
We can build \(Q\) one input at a time. A term containing \(x-2\) leaves its value at \(2\) unchanged; a term containing \((x-2)(x-4)\) leaves both earlier values unchanged. Continuing this idea gives the integer-coefficient polynomial
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q(x)={}&42-56(x-2)\\
&+28(x-2)(x-4)\\
&-8(x-2)(x-4)(x-6).
\end{aligned}
\]
Its successive terms produce exactly the four displayed values: \(42,-70,42,-6\). Now define
\[
P(x)=315+A(x)Q(x).
\]
This polynomial has integer coefficients. At each odd input \(1,3,5,7\), the factor \(A(x)\) is zero, so \(P(x)=315\). At the four even inputs, each product \(A(x)Q(x)\) equals \(-630\), so \(P(x)=-315\). Thus all eight conditions hold.

The smallest possible value is therefore \(\boxed{315}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).

Thus the integer-coefficient construction attains a=315 and proves minimality.
